input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing law/forum provision (§ 20(h)) selects Nova Scotia law and the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts — the Vendor's home jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list of New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales, so it fails the fallback on both the law and the forum. There is no arbitration clause (the only reference to arbitration fees is in the indemnity at p0090), so this is a deviation rather than walk-away, but it still requires correction. We redlined to the preferred position: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, keeping the rest of the sentence structure intact.

proposal.summary: Move governing law and venue to New York with exclusive New York County courts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Nova Scotia law and its non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our accepted position; Delaware, California or England and Wales with London courts would be an acceptable fallback.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
